items.text: {{S}} uses letters to stand for unknown numbers and recognises numbers multiplied by themselves, such as 4 × 4.
{{S}} multiplies and divides decimals accurately and works through calculations with several steps in the correct order.
{{S}} uses letters to stand for unknown numbers when solving simple problems.
{{S}} multiplies 2- and 3-digit numbers by 2-digit numbers and represents and solves division problems with whole number remainders.
{{S}} recalls multiplication facts to support calculations and solves division problems with remainders.
{{S}} creates number patterns using known multiplication facts.
{{S}} generates number patterns using times tables.
{{S}} solves division problems with whole number remainders.
{{S}} recalls some multiplication facts and uses them to support calculations.
{{S}} counts by twos, threes and fives to recognise simple division and creates equal groups to show multiplication.
{{S}} uses visual representations to find multiplication facts.
{{S}} uses strategies to solve simple division problems.
{{S}} creates and continues patterns by lining up objects according to their colour or shape.
{{S}} records how objects were shared using drawings, words and numbers.
{{S}} models and describes collections of objects as 'groups of', such as two groups of three.
{{S}} recognises and continues number patterns that increase by twos, fives, and tens past 100.
{{S}} organises objects into equal rows and columns as part of {{pos}} multiplication knowledge.
{{S}} has developed {{pos}} understanding of related multiplication and division facts.
{{S}} recognises that multiplication and division are opposites and uses one to solve the other.
{{S}} recognises that doubling a number gives the same answer as multiplying by 2.
{{S}} recalls multiplication facts up to 10 × 10 and uses them to solve worded problems.
{{S}} uses number properties, such as swapping the order of numbers, to work out related multiplication facts.
{{S}} copies a continuing pattern.
{{S}} points to or touches objects as they are shared into smaller equal groups.
{{S}} identifies the number of objects in a group.
{{S}} writes expressions with letters and finds their value by replacing letters with numbers.

Continuing repeating patterns using sounds and/or actions.
Creating repeating patterns using shapes, objects, images or pictures.
Dividing objects into smaller groups and recognising whether the number in each group is equal or not.
Grouping and sharing concrete materials by distributing objects one by one.
Modelling and describing collections of objects as 'groups of'.
Solving multiplication problems using repeated addition.
Solving multiplication and division problems using objects and diagrams.
Recording answers to multiplication and division problems using drawings, words or numerals.
Creating and continuing number patterns that increase or decrease by the same amount.
Understanding doubling is multiplying a number by two.
Relating multiplication facts to their opposite division fact.
Recalling multiplication facts up to 10 x 10.
Representing and solving multiplication and division word problems using number sentences.
Determining factors for a given whole number.
Using mental strategies to multiply one-digit numbers by 10, 100, 1000.
Solving a multiplication algorithm correctly.
Selecting and using efficient strategies to multiply whole numbers.
Solving problems involving brackets.
Providing reasoning when solving complex multiplication and division problems.
